t.6.108.1: When Kākutstha had departed, great Indra, the chastiser of Pāka, supremely pleased, spoke to Rāghava, who stood with hands joined in reverence.
t.6.108.2: O Rāma, scorcher of foes, the sight of us is never fruitless for you; I am filled with affection, therefore tell me what you desire in your heart.
t.6.108.3: Thus addressed, Kākutstha, together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa and his wife Sītā, replied with joined palms.
t.6.108.5: Those monkeys who, having fought valiantly for my sake, have gone to the abode of Yama, may they all regain their lives and rise up.
t.6.108.4: If affection for me has arisen in you, O lord of all the gods, I shall speak; make my words come true, O best of speakers.
t.6.108.6: Those who were devoted to what is dear to me and took no account of death, may they, through your grace, be reunited with their kin; this is the boon I choose.
t.6.108.8: Wherever the vānaras may dwell, there may choice roots and fruits be found even out of season, and there may the rivers be clear and pure.
t.6.108.7: O bestower of honour, I wish to see them free from sickness and free from wounds, endowed with strength and valour, the Golāṅgūla monkeys and likewise the bears.
t.6.108.9: Having heard the words of that great-souled Rāghava, the great Indra replied with these words, which bore the mark of his affection.
t.6.108.10: Great is this boon you have spoken, dear Raghunandana! The monkeys will rise up again, just as those who are asleep rise when their sleep comes to an end.
t.6.108.11: All of them, filled with supreme joy, will be reunited with their friends and kinsmen, with their relatives and their own people.
t.6.108.12: Even out of season, O great archer, the trees will be bright with many-coloured flowers and laden with fruit, and the rivers will brim with water.
t.6.108.13: With their limbs, wounded at first, now closed up and free of wounds once more, all the vānaras became astonished, asking, "What is this?"
t.6.108.14: Seeing Kākutstha, together with Lakṣmaṇa, his purpose fully accomplished, all those foremost of the gods first praised him, who was worthy of praise, and then spoke.
t.6.108.16: See your brother Bharata, who out of grief for you is practising austere vows. Have yourself consecrated as king, and, having gone there, gladden the citizens.
t.6.108.15: Go from here to Ayodhyā, O hero, and dismiss the monkeys. Console this Maithilī, who is devoted to you and has suffered so much.
t.6.108.17: Having spoken thus and taken leave of Rāma together with Saumitri, the delighted gods went to heaven in aerial chariots resplendent like the sun.
t.6.108.18: Kākutstha, together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, saluted all those foremost of the gods and then gave orders for the encampment.
t.6.108.19: Then that great and glorious army, protected by Lakṣmaṇa and Rāma, its people rejoicing, blazing with splendour, shone on every side, like the night led on by the cool-rayed moon.
